title: Concurrent Opioid Use and the First-Time Quantity Exception Ceiling
content:
**Rule (Utilization Management Program).** For a first-time quantity limit exception approved on an acute migraine drug, concurrent opioid use changes how the approval ceiling is worked out from the drug's limit times the multiple applied to it:

1. when the member's paid oxycodone-acetaminophen retail fills dated within the last three months add up to **30 or more days supply**, one unit for each average monthly opioid day — those days supply divided by 3 — is subtracted from it, a day of opioid treatment displacing one acute migraine dose;
2. when they add up to **between 1 and 29 days supply**, it is multiplied by 0.9;
3. when there is **no such fill**, it is used as it stands.

The fills read are paid retail claims for oxycodone-acetaminophen under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. The three months end on the decision date: a fill counts when dated after the same day of the month three months before the decision date. The figure this rule produces is not rounded; the approval ceiling is rounded down to a whole unit only at the end.

## Boundary table (hypothetical: limit times the multiple is 24)

| Opioid days supply in the last three months | Treatment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | as it stands | 24 |
| 1 | multiplied by 0.9 | 21.6 |
| 29 | multiplied by 0.9 | 21.6 |
| 30 | 30 divided by 3, that is 10, subtracted | 14 |
| 36 | 36 divided by 3, that is 12, subtracted | 12 |
| 40 | 40 divided by 3, about 13.333, subtracted | about 10.667 |

### Basis Q&A

**Are the days counted per fill or in total?** In total: the days supply of all paid oxycodone-acetaminophen retail fills dated in the three months is added up before the comparison with 30.

**Does a reversed opioid claim count?** Only paid fills count.
